newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville Power joins Northwest grid consortium.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville Power joins Northwest grid consortium.

text.p: A consortium of U.S. Northwest utilities announced Monday the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) agreed to join them to work for the creation of a regional independent power grid operator.

The independent grid operation, called "IndeGO," is aimed at assuring non-discriminatory, open access to electric transmission facilities, in compliance with recent Federal Energy Regulatory Commission rulings.
William Pascoe, a Montana Power Co vice president who chairs the "IndeGO" steering committee said it intends to file the independent operator proposal sometime during the first quarter of 1997.

George Bell, acting senior vice president of transmission for BPA, said BPA is most concerned with issues such as reliability, planning for changes to the transmission system, and the functions and duties of a regional operator.

BPA, as well as the other utilities, are not obligated to join IndeGO, which would serve the four Pacific Northwest states of Washington, Oregon, Idaho and Montana, as well as Nevada, Utah and Wyoming.

"Having BPA participate in this project would be significant, because BPA owns more than 11,000 miles of high-voltage transmission lines," Pascoe said. "If BPA is part of IndeGO, their participation in this project would about double the transmission mileage already represented by the seven original participants and two more recent signers of the memorandum."

After IndeGO was created by Idaho Power Co, Montana Power, PacifiCorp, Portland General Electric, Puget Sound Power & Light, Sierra Pacific, and Washington Water Power, all investor-owned utilities, it was joined by two public power entities from Washington state, Tacoma City Light, and Chelan Public Utility District.
